To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the OPC system can achieve better tolerance to nonlinear phase noise than the DC system; (b) the nonlinear phase noise tolerance is mainly determined by the dispersion slope of the transmission fiber; (c) the OPC system is more sensitive to the fiber nonlinear coefficient than the DC system.
the OPC system is superior to the periodic dispersion compensated system in reducing the nonlinear noise.
the OPC system has the potential to extend the maximum transmission distance of DPSK systems by more than 2 times that of the conventional periodic dispersion compensated system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical analysis of the nonlinear phase noise reduction in the DPSK system with OPC.
a novel method for reducing the nonlinear phase-noise accumulation in ultra long haul DPSK transmission.
the performance of optical differential phase shift keyed (DPSK) transmission in ultra long haul systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in a 10 Gb/s 10,000 km DPSK transmission, the OPC system can provide the same performance as the 50% dispersion map system, and the OPC system can be more robust to the fiber nonlinearities.

the OPC system can provide a much better performance than the DC system in the presence of nonlinear phase noise, and it can provide a much lower penalty in the presence of fiber nonlinearity than the DC system.
the nonlinear phase noise is not reduced by OPC, and the performance improvement of the OPC system is mainly from the reduced nonlinear phase jitter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear phase noise reduction by OPC is not as good as that by DC in the case of long haul DPSK transmission.
the OPC system can reduce nonlinear phase noise accumulation by more than 20dB for a 6400 km transmission, which is 5dB higher than that of periodic DC systems.
OPC is more effective in reducing the nonlinear effects in ultra long haul transmission than DC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of OPC is not only dependent on the nonlinear phase noise but also on the phase noise due to the random walk of the phase of the phase-conjugated light.
the OPC can be used to reduce nonlinear phase noise accumulation and improve the system performance in the ultra long haul transmission.
OPC has the advantage of suppressing the nonlinear phase noise in the transmission system with a much longer transmission distance.
